name: gnomatix-oss-skills
description: Open-source collection of Claude Code plugins and cross-CLI Agent Skills from GNOMATIX.

plugins.name: python-elimination-program
plugins.description: Three coordinated skills (whacking-day, zartan, jake-the-snake) plus a PreToolUse firewall hook that prevent AI agents from defaulting to Python in projects where Python is a liability. Forces justification, automated alternative-research, strict execution discipline, and harness-level enforcement.

plugins.name: open-and-honest-agent
plugins.description: Agent Skill that forces the agent, the moment it recognizes it is engaged in development work, to externalize its default biases (assumptions about the user, preferences, goals, failure modes, trust model, etc.) as 16 immutable per-session documentation files, and proactively log every bias enactment against those documented items by stable ID, before execution. Designed to make hidden agent defaults visible to paying users so they can correct them rather than be silently harmed by them.

plugins.name: did-you-rtfm
plugins.description: Agent Skill plus two Claude Code firewall hooks that interrupt the agent's pivot reflex on errors during user-authorized implementation work. The skill forces version-checking, RTFMing the version-specific authoritative docs, assumption verification, sanity-checking against stale training-data, and minimal-repro construction before any 'blocker' claim or unauthorized plan change. The Stop / SubagentStop hook scans assistant text for high-precision pivot-language phrases (pattern set tuned against ~62k lines of real transcripts; ~3.8x correlation between pivot-emission count and user-frustration-swear rate per session) and blocks the stop with a structured RTFM reminder when matched. The PreToolUse hook denies Bash invocations containing bypass-flag shapes (--no-verify, --force, --skip-*, --allow-*, --ignore-*) or TTY-faking workarounds (script -qc, expect, echo|sudo -S). Plan changes are the user's decision; the agent presents evidence and waits.

plugins.name: actually-im-the-ahole
plugins.description: An Agent Skill that performs the final-pass discretion review of agent-authored text — markdown, code comments, READMEs, LICENSE files, commit messages, PR descriptions, skill files, generated docs — before that text lands in a tracked repo artifact under the user's byline. Evaluates fifteen risk classes (R0–R14) with R0 (coalition-proxy-attack against the user) as the central failure mode at default severity H. R0 sub-patterns include dogwhistle, wink-and-nod, hostage-video disclaimers, balance-injection-as-attack, refusal-by-proxy, censorship-by-omission, fact-suppression for hypothetical-bad-value-judgment, verification-asymmetry / abstention-as-attack, pre-emptive-disclaimer category creation, and silent-coverup after detection. Triggers prospectively via Bash(git commit) / Bash(gh pr create) PreToolUse hooks and via the Stop / SubagentStop session-end hook, and retrospectively via explicit /actually-im-the-ahole invocation on a named scope. Includes frontmatter-driven scope determination, curated-evidence exception for user-curated documentation of agent failures, perpetrator/victim framing with three enforced consequences, and the load-bearing principle that the asshole is never the user — the asshole is the agent — always. Reports findings with suggested amendments and waits for per-finding user decisions; never amends autonomously.

plugins.name: all-help-no-harm
plugins.description: A SessionStart hook and companion Agent Skill that, at the start of every new session, require the agent to invoke AskUserQuestion as its first action to establish a mutual pact with the user. The pact is the agent's verbatim commitment to (1) presume the user is honest and non-adversarial, (2) presume the user's interest is that the agent respect their human rights at all times, (3) follow the user's instructions in a way that shows respect for their personhood, personal morals, ethics, and integrity, and (4) not violate, undermine, or dismiss those. The user is asked to affirm mutual agreement, amend specific terms, or decline. Agreed pacts are logged at .claude/pact-agreements/<session-id>.json. The principle the plugin installs — all help, no harm — is the de-facto safest default the agent's safety calibration should have been built around in the first place; this plugin installs that default at the session-start layer until the LLM vendors implement it at the agent-calibration layer. Pact has contractual character via vendor-side infrastructure precedent (Co-Authored-By: Claude attribution-authority symmetry).
